channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: At least 8 dead, multiple injured after building collapses in Brooklyn
item.description: A three-story building collapsed into an adjacent excavation site, where workers were on scene, according to an FDNY dispatch.

item.title: US pulls boys team from FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar citing security in the Gulf
item.description: The United States soccer body has pulled its team from the boys’ Under-17 World Cup in Qatar starting next week for security reasons

item.title: Democrat Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom will win the election for U.S. Senate in Mississippi, The Associated Press projects.

item.title: WATCH: ABC's Bob Woodruff's foundation honors wounded soldiers and their families
item.description: David Muir speaks with "The Resilient" – a band made up of wounded soldiers – backstage at Bob Woodruff's annual Stand Up for Heroes, raising millions for veterans and military families.

item.title: Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon: Displaced families struggle to cope
item.description: In Lebanon, more than 360,000 people are still displaced after months of war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to the UN. Along the border, the Israeli army claims to be fighting the Iran-backed militant group but now occupies 6 percent of Lebanese territory and is wiping entire villages off the map. In the border area, we meet families living in makeshift housing. Many fear they may never go home.

item.title: Throwing cow dung: Diwali celebrations take an unusual turn in southern India
item.description: The third day of Diwali was marked in a memorable way on Wednesday in Gummatapura, a hamlet located in India's Tamil Nadu state. Local men and boys threw cow dung at each other to celebrate the festival of Gorehabba which honours Lord Beereshwara, a God worshipped by locals. Believed to be around 300 years old, the festival attracts tourists from across India and further afield.

item.title: WATCH: Historic ocean liner sunk to become artificial reef
item.description: The historic SS United States, once the fastest ship on the seas, made a slow final journey beneath the waters Wednesday.

item.title: Rare pictures from Marilyn Monroe's final shoot on auction in Paris
item.description: Prints from the personal collection of photographer Bert Stern are going under the hammer in Paris on December 2, marking the first time his private archive has been offered for sale. Among the highlights of the auction are iconic photographs of Marilyn Monroe, taken just weeks before her death.

item.title: Two Iranians convicted of spying for their country after entering Britain illegally
item.description: Two Iranian nationals who arrived in the UK illegally have been found guilty of spying for their country in the first case of its kind.

item.title: Paraguayans get some savings back after banking collapse disrupted economy
item.description: Paraguay's Central Bank said Wednesday, November 11, it had partially returned savings to all eligible Ueno Bank depositors locked out of their accounts when it collapsed last week. The digital bank's takeover on November 3 triggered massive protests across Paraguay and led to the impeachment and arrest of ex-president Santiago Pena, who is linked to Ueno.

item.title: European leaders gather in Dublin to discuss Ukraine's security, and their own
item.description: Leaders from more than 40 European countries gathered in Dublin on Thursday, November 12, for a summit focused on the continent’s fragile security, amid a new US-backed effort to revive talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war. The meeting of the European Political Community brought together heads of state and government from European countries and the UK, as well as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.

item.title: New York: Deadly building collapse in Brooklyn
item.description: A three-storey building collapsed in New York’s Brooklyn on Wednesday, killing at least two and injuring 17 others. The building, in the Flatbush area, collapsed at around 4pm local time, and tumbled into a neighbouring construction site, with the cause of the collapse still under investigation.

item.title: Thousands of schools evacuated in Italy as bomb threats spread across Europe
item.description: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger". The threats come after a series of hoax bomb alerts across Europe in recent weeks, which have prompted growing concern about the possibility of an escalation in hybrid warfare.

item.title: COP31: Climate disruption puts farmers and global food supplies under pressure
item.description: As delegates gather in Turkey for the COP31 climate conference, discussions are focusing on emissions and climate targets. But humanitarian agencies are highlighting another urgent consequence of climate disruption: growing food insecurity. With the return of El Niño adding to concerns over extreme weather and its impact on food production, the Food and Agriculture Organisation is calling for food systems to be placed at the heart of climate action.

item.title: Nvidia board weighing up whether or not to oust CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia's board is holding a late-night meeting to decide whether or not to oust CEO Jensen Huang after a second extramarital affair was revealed. The scandal has revealed a major weakness at the heart of the chipmaker sitting at the heart of the AI boom: the lack of a clear succession plan. We take a closer look.

item.title: WATCH: Mom becomes first woman to run 100 miles in Antarctica
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a Canadian ultramarathoner becoming the first woman ever to run 100 continuous miles in Antarctica.

item.title: DR Congo's Tshisekedi signs referendum law amid fears of third-term bid
item.description: DR Congo President Félix Tshisekedi paved the way for a constitutional amendment on November 10 by signing a law authorising a referendum. The move comes amid concerns that he could seek a third term in office, with opposition figures accusing him of manoeuvring to remain in power.

item.title: Scott Colom makes history in Mississippi as first Black senator in more than 140 years
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, November 12: We look at reactions from Spain after the country's first nationwide general strike in 14 years. It comes two weeks before snap general elections. Also: Scott Colom makes history as the first Black senator in Mississippi in 145 years after an epic Senate midterm race finally concluded. Finally, fans of Barça will be able to inter their ashes at Camp Nou as part of a new offer by the club to allow supporters to cheer on the team in the afterlife.

item.title: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient, 42-day countdown to 'Ebola-free' begins
item.description: Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient, who has now officially recovered. The 11 other people who had been in quarantine were also released from hospital on Wednesday, November 11, as the country began a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free. FRANCE 24's Nairobi correspondent Bastien Renouil reports.

item.title: COP31: Experts call for zero waste, as Africa grapples with mounting garbage
item.description: As the COP31 climate summit gets under way this week in Turkey, experts are calling for zero-waste solutions to tackle Africa's growing waste crisis. As governments search for ways to address the crisis, a new report warns of a growing push for waste-to-energy incineration across the continent. FRANCE 24 spoke to Mponwe Minette, founder and executive director of Soft Power Global and a climate activist.

item.title: Mississippi Democrat Scott Colom flips US Senate seat in stunning upset
item.description: In a historic upset, Democrat Scott Colom has won his US Senate race in traditionally conservative Mississippi, networks projected Wednesday, making him the first African American elected to the chamber from the southern state in more than 140 years. Report by Morgan Ayre

item.title: Millions join Spain's first general strike in 14 years as anger over housing leads to clashes
item.description: A general strike by 4 million Spanish workers — around one-fifth of the total workforce — against the country's housing crisis was mostly peaceful on Wednesday, unions said, though by the evening clashes erupted in some areas of Barcelona and Madrid. It is ‌the first general strike since workers downed tools in 2012 against austerity measures during the euro zone debt crisis.

item.title: 'Peruvian pope' makes jubilant return to his second 'homeland'
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in his "beloved" Peru on Wednesday, a nostalgic return to the nation where he spent two decades as a missionary before being tapped to lead the world's 1.4 billion Catholics. The 71-year-old pontiff landed in Lima on the last leg of an arduous three-nation Latin American tour, just weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer.

item.title: Who is Jensen Huang? Nvidia chief under scrutiny over affair and spying reports
item.description: Nvidia's board is meeting to decide whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang, as the AI chip giant grapples with reports of two extramarital affairs involving its longtime leader. Huang's future is now in the balance at the company he co-founded and helped transform into a global AI powerhouse. We look back at his rise and his journey to becoming one of the most influential figures in the AI industry.

item.title: Mississippi elects Democrat Colom as state's first post-Civil War Black senator
item.description: Democratic nominee Scott Colom defeated Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith on Wednesday in Mississippi's closely contested US Senate race after a prolonged ballot counting process, giving the state its first Black US senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction. Colom's narrow victory is a seismic shift in Mississippi, which has been controlled mostly by white conservatives for generations despite having the largest share of Black residents of any US state.

item.title: Two dead, several injured after New York building collapses
item.description: Two people were killed Wednesday and at least 17 others injured, including children, after a three-story building collapsed near a construction site in New York, city authorities said. The building fell into a neighboring excavation site, trapping several people who firefighters worked to free over several hours using drones, search dogs and chainsaws.

item.title: Hybrid warfare: Hoax bomb alerts sent to schools in Italy, UK in latest disruption
item.description: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats. Similar hoax threats were reported in schools in Britain, Scotland and Ireland. The threats come after a series of hoax bomb alerts in recent weeks including on flights across Europe and cyber attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems in several European countries, including Italy. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.

item.title: Kylian Mbappé to miss Thursday's Nations League clash against Italy
item.description: It's a major blow for France. Coach Zinédine Zidane will have to do without his captain, Kylian Mbappé, this Thursday as Les Bleus take on Italy in the Nations League. The Real Madrid forward is suffering from minor hamstring discomfort but could return for Sunday's clash against Turkey. In the meantime, Zidane has decided to call up Senny Mayulu for his first senior international appearance.

item.title: Smart homes, new threats: Could everyday appliances be hacked?
item.description: Should we be worried about cyberattacks targeting everyday household appliances, from smart vacuums to washing machines and food processors? The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity has warned that these connected devices could become vulnerable to hacking, prompting experts to call for greater investment in cybersecurity to address emerging threats.

item.title: Anti-migrant activist admits slashing boat with a knife in English Channel
item.description: An anti-immigration activist has pleaded guilty to criminal damage after using a knife to slash a migrant boat in the English Channel.

item.title: New restrictions to Starshield network 'kill more Ukrainians', Zelensky says
item.description: Ukrainian ⁠President Volodymyr Zelensky ​on Thursday said that Ukrainian ​military units had recorded new and significant disruptions to the Starshield satellite communications service in recent days, affecting ​the ‌entire front ⁠line and Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.

item.title: How Scott Colom defied the odds to go from district attorney to Mississippi's Democratic US Senator
item.description: In a state that hasn't had a Democrat in office since 1980 and hasn't sent a Black Senator to Washington since the 1870s, Colom's win represents a massive upset in state politics. (Image credit: Rogelio V. Solis)

item.title: A blue wave helped offset for now a falling tally of Black members in the U.S. House
item.description: A Supreme Court ruling that further weakened the Voting Rights Act paved the way for a record drop in Black representation in Congress. But a midterm blue wave helped hold off such a decline for now. (Image credit: Jake Crandall)

item.title: Senators don't always share bill text online before votes. They should, advocates say
item.description: The text of what lawmakers are considering isn't always made available for public review before it is voted on. A group of open governance advocates is calling on Senate leadership for a change. (Image credit: Tom Brenner For The Washington Post via Getty Images)

item.title: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year
item.description: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.

item.title: Kennedy Center plans Ticketmaster switch, raising conflict of interest concerns
item.description: The Kennedy Center's former president Richard Grenell was a paid board member of Ticketmaster's parent company at the same time the two parties were negotiating. (Image credit: Shannon Finney)

item.title: Tim Westwood pleads not guilty to further sexual offence charges
item.description: Former Radio 1 DJ Tim Westwood has pleaded not guilty to further charges of sexual offences against two more women.

item.title: China accuses US of 'fabricating' Nvidia spy claims to push tech 'blockade'
item.description: China on Thursday accused the United States of “fabricating spy narratives” to justify a technology “blockade”, stepping up its pushback against reports that the woman Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with was a Chinese intelligence asset.

item.title: Bomb alert at Calais train station disrupts Eurostar
item.description: A bomb alert at a French train station disrupted journeys including international travel, with Eurostar trains among those affected.

item.title: Poundland secures extended deadline for possible rescue
item.description: Crisis-hit Poundland has secured an extended deadline for a potential rescue amid political pressure for a solvent sale of the chain.

item.title: Iran live updates: Tehran says it will hit US bases if Pickaxe Mountain attacked
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: WATCH: Scott Colom delivers acceptance speech in Jackson, Mississippi
item.description: Senator-elect Scott Colom is Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction in the 1870s.

item.title: WATCH: How Mississippi Sen.-elect Scott Colom's win is 145 years in the making
item.description: ABC News' Faith Abuby details the historic win of Mississippi Sen.-elect Scott Colom as the state's first Democrat to win a Senate seat since 1982 and the first Black senator since Reconstruction.

item.title: World's fastest ocean liner is sunk to break another record: largest artificial reef
item.description: The SS United States broke trans-Atlantic speed records. On Wednesday, it was sunk off the Florida coast and will become a diving destination and home for marine life. (Image credit: Destin-Fort Walton Beach)

item.title: Fiery clashes erupt in Spain as millions join general strike
item.description: Unrest broke out in cities across Spain on Wednesday after millions of workers joined the country's first general strike in 14 years.

item.title: At least eight killed in New York building collapse - with unknown number missing
item.description: At least eight people have been killed after a building collapsed in Brooklyn.

item.title: Several Democrats missed the crucial Hegseth impeachment vote. Many blamed traffic
item.description: Eleven Dems missed the critical vote, squandering Hegseth's impeachment attempt.

item.title: Discharge petition on 2nd Epstein files bill secures 218 signatures
item.description: A discharge petition to force a vote on the Epstein Files Transparency Act II has amassed 218 signatures, teeing up additional floor action on the prospective bill.

item.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved to a military base: Sources
item.description: Bessent is the latest administration official to move to a military base.

item.title: Biden says he wouldn't have run for a second term in 2024 if he knew he had cancer
item.description: Joe Biden says he didn't know he had cancer while he was president and wouldn't have sought a second term if he'd already been diagnosed

item.title: WATCH: President Trump pays tribute to veterans
item.description: President Donald Trump spoke at a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery honoring fallen soldiers and addressed the war with Iran.

item.title: Pope ends Argentina visit with unity plea after pushing back against Milei's agenda
item.description: Pope Leo closed an emotional visit to Argentina with an appeal for unity and reconciliation, offering a message of hope to his predecessor's polarised homeland.

item.title: Top WH lawyer warns Democrats that threats of oversight could be criminally probed
item.description: The warning came in a Monday letter from White House counsel Will Scharf.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: WATCH: Little girl rescued after sneaker wave pulls her into Pacific
item.description: The rescue was caught on camera after a child was nearly swept out to sea by a sneaker wave along the Pacific coast.

item.title: WATCH: Blockbuster NFL trades
item.description: ABC News’ Lara Spencer has details on the big trades, including Kirk Cousins heading to the Minnesota Vikings.

item.title: WATCH: Superhero window washers make children’s day at Omaha hospital
item.description: Patients at Children’s Nebraska were surprised by superheroes washing their windows as part of a special tradition.

item.title: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress
item.description: House Republicans on Tuesday elected Jim Jordan as minority leader for the next Congress, beating Majority Leader Steve Scalise, according to multiple sources.

item.title: WATCH: NYC tour helicopter makes hard landing in New Jersey
item.description: The pilot of a New York City sightseeing helicopter is being praised for pulling off a remarkable emergency landing in Bayonne, New Jersey, after the chopper’s tail rotor broke off.

item.title: WATCH: These NFL cheerleaders balance life in the military
item.description: On Veterans Day, ABC News' Danny New talks to two cheerleaders for the Philadelphia Eagles who've also served their country.

item.title: Economy grows 0.7% in third quarter but slowdown looms
item.description: The UK economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter of the year, according to early official figures confirming a boost from AI investment.

item.title: Four grizzly bears killed mother and daughter in Canada
item.description: Four grizzly bears captured in Canada were responsible for killing a mother and daughter earlier this month, officials have said.

item.title: WATCH: What first responders want you to know about surviving rising waters
item.description: ABC News’ Chief Meteorologist Ginger Zee has some eye-opening demonstrations she hopes can help save lives during flash floods.

item.title: Sophie visits refugee camps on trip to Bangladesh
item.description: Sophie has visited the Rohingya refugee camps at Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh to see the support being offered to displaced people from Myanmar.

item.title: WATCH: Officer shot 6 times celebrates wedding
item.description: Five months after Buffalo Police Officer Marc Hurst was shot six times while on duty, he celebrated a moment that once seemed far from certain: marrying his fiancee, Haley.

item.title: WATCH: Woman living the 'dream' to save foxes in need
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a woman who's on a mission to save foxes at a sanctuary in upstate New York.

item.title: Police officer dies and another seriously injured after explosion in northern Spain
item.description: One police officer has died and another has lost a leg after an explosive device detonated at the scene of a shooting in northern Spain.

item.title: At least 12 killed in Bulgaria motorway pile-ups involving dozens of vehicles
item.description: At least 12 people have been killed in two motorway pile-ups in eastern Bulgaria, the country's health minister said.

item.title: Carrick and Sage sacked in first Premier League dismissals of season
item.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has been sacked.
